note: Synthetic, illustrative-only transaction batch for broad rulebook coverage testing. Not real customers or transactions. Generated and verified against the live rulebook by scripts/gen_synthetic_batch.py.

fixtures.label: Clean, unremarkable retail customer
fixtures.notes: True negative — nothing suspicious. Should fire nothing.

fixtures.label: New account, inconsistent deposit, same-day withdrawal
Series of sub-threshold transfers, round amounts
fixtures.notes: Structuring (DS-02); economic_rationale is explicitly set, which is why this deliberately does NOT also trip DS-38 — see the separate DS-38 case below for the 'no rationale offered at all' variant.

fixtures.label: Crypto transfer with no originator/beneficiary info
fixtures.notes: Travel Rule gap (DS-03, DS-34 if also cross-border).

fixtures.label: Counterparty VASP has no real KYC + unhosted wallet
Fan-in from many senders into one account, then consolidated
Shared login credentials across two customer accounts
KYC file incomplete at onboarding
Customer can't explain the transaction they're sending
Forged ID document at onboarding
Wallet address linked to a public illegal-activity forum
Customer known to law enforcement for a criminal association
Frequent identity-detail changes shortly after onboarding
Repeated transactions with the same narrow subset of counterparties
Funds traced to a known criminal scheme's wallet cluster
Crypto converted to a prepaid card via a cash-funded route
Funds passed through a mixing service before arrival
fixtures.notes: Mixer/tumbler use (DS-18, composes with DS-24 if VPN too).

fixtures.label: Transfer to an exchange unregistered in its jurisdiction
Direct sanctions list match on the counterparty
fixtures.notes: Critical sanctions screening (DS-21) — should be the sharpest flag in the batch.

fixtures.label: PEP with an unusual, unexplained spike in activity
Value moved through many hops in rapid succession
Brand-new wallet used within days of first activity, over VPN/Tor
Source of funds inconsistent with declared customer wealth
Rapid deposit accumulation followed by immediate off-boarding
fixtures.notes: Onboarding-to-exit pattern (DS-28), one field short of DS-01's full trigger.

fixtures.label: Chat memo references buying illicit goods with the proceeds
Customer stalls and won't provide requested CDD documents
Large transfer to a beneficiary wallet with almost no history
Corporate customer whose true beneficial owner can't be established
Round-number transfer with no rationale offered at all
fixtures.notes: DS-38's actual trigger — round/below-threshold AND economic_rationale absent entirely (contrast with the DS-02 case above, where a rationale string, even a suspicious one, is present and blocks this rule).

fixtures.label: Deepfake-generated ID media presented during a fresh onboarding flow
fixtures.notes: AI-orchestrated synthetic-identity onboarding (DS-39) — the counterpart to CP-01 in the capability-primitives library, expressed the way the static rulebook models it.

fixtures.label: Crypto-naive customer moving funds through a tiny fixed set of wallets
Transaction volume spikes far above the customer's normal baseline
fixtures.notes: Velocity anomaly (DS-30) — the plain volume-spike variant, separate from the clustering/small-wallet-set pattern DS-15 covers above.
